title: Format Converter
description: Preview and convert real microscopy files into spaCR-compatible Yokogawa TIFF names with a reversible provenance map.
objectives: Choose a microscope-image source tree, destination, layout, Z handling, and plate naming scheme.
Audit the complete source-to-target mapping before any output is written.
Convert atomically, inspect the provenance map, and resume without rewriting completed fields.
prerequisite: A folder containing ND2, CZI, LIF, OME-TIFF, TIFF, PNG, JPEG, or BMP microscopy images.

scenes.narration: Format Converter turns vendor or general microscopy images into the Yokogawa-style TIFF names that spaCR Mask and Measure read directly. Open it from Data and batch runs. The central safety rule is preview first and convert second.
scenes.speech_text: Format Converter turns vendor or general microscopy images into the Yokogawa style TIFF names that spacer Mask and Measure read directly. Open it from Data and batch runs. The central safety rule is preview first and convert second.

scenes.narration: Drop a source folder or choose it here, then select a new destination. This demonstration uses two real four-channel fields from the transferred experiment. Their pixels were copied byte-for-byte; only the tutorial folder structure and source filenames were prepared for this conversion example.
scenes.speech_text: Drop a source folder or choose it here, then select a new destination. This demonstration uses two real four channel fields from the transferred experiment. scenes.narration: Layout describes whether images sit directly in the source, below well folders, or below plate and well folders; automatic detection is normally appropriate. Keep every Z plane is the lossless default. Max projection and first-plane mode explicitly discard planes. Plate names may be sequential or preserve source folders, and Resume validates field checkpoints before skipping them.

scenes.narration: With automatic layout detection, lossless Z handling, sequential plate names, and the new destination selected, click Preview. Preview scans headers and builds the mapping but does not create the destination or write an image.

scenes.narration: The complete eight-file plan appears before conversion. Each row places its recognizable source beside the exact target, plate, well, field, channel, Z, time, original identifiers, and status. The first output is plate1, A01, field 1, channel 1; the last is field 2, channel 4. The status confirms that nothing has been written.

scenes.narration: Review the summary and click Convert only when the mapping is correct. A collision disables this button rather than overwriting a target. Valid files are written atomically to the separate destination, so the original microscopy images are never renamed or replaced.

scenes.narration: All eight TIFFs were written successfully. conversion_map.csv records every target beside its original absolute and relative path, source identifiers, spaCR join identifiers, dimensions, Z policy, and metadata. The prepared source TIFF hashes remain byte-identical after conversion.

scenes.narration: Enable Resume for an interrupted or repeated conversion. Resume does not trust filenames alone: it consults an atomic field checkpoint and validates every TIFF belonging to a completed field before deciding that the field can be skipped.
scenes.speech_text: Enable Resume for an interrupted or repeated conversion. Resume does not trust filenames alone: it consults an atomic field checkpoint and validates every TIFF belonging to a completed field before deciding that the field can be skipped.

scenes.narration: Click Convert again with the same verified plan and Resume enabled. If one file were missing or corrupt, its entire field would be rebuilt; complete fields can be reused safely.

scenes.narration: Both four-channel fields pass validation, so Resume writes zero files and reports two resumed fields. The eight-row provenance map and eight converted TIFFs remain complete, finishing a reversible, lossless, and restart-safe import into spaCR naming.
